page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The statement
lines: The principle of homogeneity states that every
term on both sides of a correct physical
equation must have the same dimensions.
steps.why: Quantities of different kinds cannot be added, in the same way that a length cannot be added to a time. The principle is that fact written as a rule.
common_mistakes: Saying the two sides must be equal in value. The principle is about dimensions, not numbers.

recall.must_convey: That every term on both sides of a correct equation must have the same dimensions.

steps.memory_tip: You cannot add a length to a time. That is the whole principle.

steps.why: The check is one-way. It can prove an equation false but never prove it true, because a missing factor of ½ or 2π leaves the dimensions untouched.
common_mistakes: Saying a dimensionally correct equation must be correct. The constant is invisible to this test.

recall.must_convey: That it is used to check equations and find unknown units, but cannot prove an equation is right.

steps.memory_tip: It can prove an equation WRONG, never prove it right — the ½ is invisible.
steps.margin_note: The one-way nature of the check is worth one line.
